it still failes.

need to be defined before you call 'inla.coxph'

so something else is going on

x$ttZ1 <- x$Z1

data = c(list(inla_y = inla_y, x)),
control.hazard=list(model="rw2", scale.model=TRUE))

messages.author: 953deaf1a512b96e
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Fitting a Cox model with a time-based interaction gives error 'breaks' not unique
parts:
Hi Nadeesha,

The error comes from the fact that the weight for time dependent covariates that you are using comes from the baseline hazard intervals [a,b]. You have to use the middle of the interval for an appropriate weight and in your code you are using the value 'a'. Therefore for the first interval, the log of the weight is then the log of zero (=Inf). I fixed it in the attached code.

Now about the error about the breaks not unique, I think it is because you have very few observations so in some situations the "middle breaks" returned by inla.group can have the same value as minimum or maximum values. I also fixed it in the attached code.

Best,
Denis Rustand
he...@r-inla.org

messages.author: 10edd14eaa782c14
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Fitting a Cox model with a time-based interaction gives error 'breaks' not unique
parts:
Hi Denis,

Thank you for the updated code and insight into what is happening. There is a reason I took 'a' as the weight instead of the interval mid-point. I noticed that the parameter estimates for the interaction terms are slightly biased, and it overinflates Type-I error. If I take 'a' instead of the interval mid-point, then that reduces the bias. So far, this approach has worked without any issues.

Yesterday, I went through my code again and realized that I had made an error in simulating the data. Once I corrected the error, the code ran without any issues.

Thank you,
Nadeesha
